A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same NoisyGRPO paper, with complete main text, references, and Appendices A-D. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content except for the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its associated link.

before.justification: v1 reports original NoisyGRPO training and benchmark results for Qwen2.5-VL 3B and 7B, alongside ablations, statistical analyses, qualitative examples, and data-scaling experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices B-D, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and data-scaling experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical noise-injected rollout generation, clean-input policy updates, reward functions, and Bayesian advantage estimation. No algorithm, objective, or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use MM-RLHF VQA training data and evaluate MME-CoT, MMStar, AMBER, and MME-RealWorld-Lite. The appendix experiments retain the same tasks and data coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical throughout: GRPO and reference models in Table 1, base models/SFT/GRPO and reference models in Table 2, component variants in Figure 4, and ROUGE versus SBERT rewards in Table 5.

E3.justification: The model sizes, four-rollout setting, training data, hyperparameters, evaluation metrics, and testing procedures remain identical. Appendix D retains the same randomly sampled 3k/6k subsets and equal-training-step comparison.

E4.justification: Both retain identical component ablations, hyperparameter and noise-distribution analyses, reward comparisons, Gaussian-residual checks, qualitative examples, and data-scaling analyses in Section 4.6 and Appendices B-D.

E5.justification: Variance shading and its descriptions in Figures 1 and 3 are unchanged. Appendix B.2 retains the same Shapiro-Wilk and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests; no run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including appendix results. Both report 3B MME-CoT F1 of 40.6 versus GRPO's 36.2 in Table 1 and MMStar averages of 58.2 versus 54.5 in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations 1-16, the Gaussian assumptions, variance specification, Bayesian posterior derivation, and appendix residual reasoning are identical. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, or derivations change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about noise-driven exploration, Bayesian advantage estimation, improved generalization and robustness, and particular benefits for small-scale MLLMs.

C2.justification: The explanations of grounded reasoning, efficiency and coverage tradeoffs, training dynamics, and appendix findings remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitation concerning weak noise-correctness correlation in coarse-grained perception.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, hyperparameters, SBERT reward details, eight-A100 hardware, training times, and the project-page link are unchanged. The updated arXiv version link adds no code, data, or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning passages elsewhere, and all 65 numbered reference entries are identical. No cited work or novelty relationship is added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 24 Oct 2025 to v3 dated 7 Apr 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology, and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1-13, Tables 1-6, equations, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2-22 render identically; the first-page visual difference is confined to the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: v3 reproduces the same scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, reproducibility information, and presentation, including Appendices A-D. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and associated link does not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's quality.
